verdict.rationale: Maritime's own web-apps feature serves any Dockerfile repo on a public, no-login HTTPS URL, so a service running inside a Maritime-run container is reachable publicly. However, nothing documents exposing an arbitrary port from an agent's sandbox or micro-VM as a preview URL. missing for 10: port selection or exposure from a running agent sandbox, preview-URL lifecycle and access controls, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can expose a port from the sandbox on a public preview URL to reach services running inside

citations.quote: Any repo with a Dockerfile can be served on a public, no-login HTTPS URL. Maritime builds it, runs it serverlessly, puts it to sleep when idle, and wakes it on the next visit.
